quests.question: My sister ___ coffee every morning.
quests.hint: A single person ('my sister') needs the verb with -s.
quests.explanation: Third-person singular subjects (he, she, it, a single person or thing) require the verb to add -s or -es in the simple present.

quests.question: My sisters ___ coffee every morning.
quests.hint: More than one person ('my sisters') takes the base form of the verb.
quests.explanation: Plural subjects never add -s to the verb in the simple present. 'My sisters drink' is correct because 'sisters' is plural.

quests.question: The dog ___ loudly at strangers.
quests.hint: One dog is singular; singular subjects need a verb ending in -s.
quests.explanation: 'The dog' is a singular noun, so the verb must be 'barks' - adding -s to show agreement with a third-person singular subject.

quests.question: The children ___ in the park after school.
quests.hint: 'Children' is already a plural noun - no -s is needed on the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Children' is the irregular plural of 'child'. Like all plural nouns, it takes the base form of the verb: 'play', not 'plays'.

quests.question: The teacher ___ the lesson every day.
quests.hint: One teacher is a single, third-person subject - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The teacher' is singular, so the verb takes the third-person singular ending: 'prepares'. The -s moves from the noun to the verb.

quests.question: The students ___ their assignments online.
quests.hint: A group of students is plural - use the base form of the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The students' is plural, so the verb stays in its base form: 'submit'. Adding -s would be wrong because the subject is not singular.

quests.question: She ___ the bus to work every weekday.
quests.hint: 'She' is a singular pronoun - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: The pronouns he, she, and it are all third-person singular and require a verb ending in -s or -es in the simple present.

quests.question: They ___ the bus together every weekday.
quests.hint: 'They' is plural - no -s on the verb.
quests.explanation: 'They' is a plural pronoun, so the verb must stay in its base form: 'take'. 'Takes' would only be correct for a singular subject.

quests.question: The cat ___ on the sofa all afternoon.
quests.hint: One cat is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The cat' is a singular subject, so the verb takes the -s ending: 'sleeps'. This rule applies to any singular noun in third person.

quests.question: He ___ at the hospital five days a week.
quests.hint: 'He' is singular - the verb needs the -s ending.
quests.explanation: Third-person singular pronouns (he, she, it) always take a verb with -s in the simple present: 'he works', not 'he work'.

quests.question: The nurses ___ long shifts at the hospital.
quests.hint: Multiple nurses is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The nurses' is plural, so the verb takes its base form: 'work'. The -s ending belongs to singular subjects, not plural ones.

quests.question: The market ___ at six in the morning.
quests.hint: One market is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The market' is a single thing (singular), so the verb must be 'opens'. Any singular noun in third person requires a verb ending in -s.

quests.question: The café ___ excellent sandwiches at lunchtime.
quests.hint: One café is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The café' is a singular noun, so the verb is 'serves' - adding -s to show third-person singular agreement.

quests.question: The cafés along this street ___ excellent sandwiches.
quests.hint: More than one café makes a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The cafés' is plural, so the verb stays as 'serve'. Plural subjects never take the -s ending in the simple present.

quests.question: My phone ___ a lot of storage.
quests.hint: One phone is a singular thing - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'My phone' is a singular noun, so the verb must be 'uses'. This is the standard third-person singular rule applied to objects.

quests.question: The app ___ your location to give directions.
quests.hint: One app is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The app' is a singular noun (it), so the verb takes the -s ending: 'tracks'. Any singular thing takes this form in the simple present.

quests.question: Both apps ___ your location automatically.
quests.hint: 'Both apps' is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'Both apps' is plural, so the verb is 'track'. 'Both' always signals a plural subject in English.

quests.question: The pilot ___ the plane carefully through the storm.
quests.hint: One pilot is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The pilot' is singular, so the verb must be 'guides'. Singular subjects in third person always take a verb with -s in the simple present.

quests.question: The passengers ___ their seatbelts during takeoff.
quests.hint: Multiple passengers is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The passengers' is plural, so the verb is 'fasten'. Adding -s would be incorrect because there is more than one person.

quests.question: This film ___ a lot of expensive special effects.
quests.hint: One film is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'This film' is singular, so the verb is 'requires'. Singular subjects take a verb with -s; plural subjects take the base form.

quests.question: These films ___ a lot of expensive special effects.
quests.hint: 'These films' is plural - use the base form of the verb.
quests.explanation: 'These films' is plural, so the verb stays as 'require'. The -s ending is only for singular subjects in third person.

quests.question: The manager ___ the weekly report every Friday.
quests.hint: One manager is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The manager' is a singular noun, so the verb takes -s: 'sends'. This is the core rule: singular subject → verb + -s.

quests.question: The managers ___ their reports to the director.
quests.hint: Multiple managers is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The managers' is plural, so the verb stays as 'send'. Plural subjects always take the base form of the verb in simple present.

quests.question: This recipe ___ two cups of flour.
quests.hint: One recipe is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'This recipe' is singular, so the verb is 'needs'. The -s signals agreement with a third-person singular subject.

quests.question: The gym ___ at five in the morning on weekdays.
quests.hint: One place (the gym) is singular - add -s or -es.
quests.explanation: 'The gym' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'opens'. Any singular noun or pronoun in third person requires this form.

quests.question: Both gyms ___ early on weekday mornings.
quests.hint: 'Both gyms' is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'Both gyms' is plural, so the verb is 'open'. 'Both' always makes the subject plural, and plural subjects take the base form.

quests.question: The artist ___ her paintings at local galleries.
quests.hint: One artist is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The artist' is singular, so the verb must be 'exhibits' - adding -s for third-person singular agreement.

quests.question: The supermarket ___ fresh bread every morning.
quests.hint: One supermarket is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The supermarket' is a singular noun, so the verb takes -s: 'bakes'. This is the basic rule for third-person singular subjects.

quests.question: The local supermarkets ___ fresh bread daily.
quests.hint: 'The local supermarkets' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The supermarkets' is plural, so the verb is 'bake'. No -s is added when the subject is plural.

quests.question: He ___ his emails as soon as he wakes up.
quests.hint: 'He' is a singular pronoun - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: The pronouns 'he', 'she', and 'it' are all singular, so the verb takes -s: 'he checks', not 'he check'.
